S9.01.needs: a folder with files in it
S9.01.note: Only the file mention picker was found; no project, model or skill picker in this list.
steps: In the message box, type @ and wait for the Files list to open.
Type a few letters of a file name and watch the list narrow.
Press Enter to insert the chosen file into the message, or Esc to cancel.
Compare: the list narrows as you type. It lists workspace files only; no projects, models or skills appear in this list.
S9.01.where: Type @ in the message box (the Files list opens)

steps: In the message box, type /model and press Enter.
Use the up and down arrows to choose a model.
Press Enter to switch to it; a line reading Model changed to appears in the chat.
Compare: the conversation now uses the chosen model. Tab or the left and right arrows change the effort level.
S9.02.where: Type /model and press Enter (opens the Models box)

S9.04.needs: a connector with more than one linked account
S9.04.note: No account picker found. Searched apps/cli/src for account picker, select account, linked account and account_id; the only hit was an account check in apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_workspaces.rs.

labels.text: Browse and create the projects in your AGI account.
Link this directory to an account project by id or name.

S9.06.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one project
S9.06.note: This is a command, not an in-app picker. Expected says chats or tasks run in the project; I did not confirm that link effect in code.
steps: In a terminal, type agi projects list and press Enter to see your account's projects.
Change into the folder you want, then type agi projects link <project name or id>.
Compare: the command reports the link. The project is typed by name or id; no list selection was found.
S9.06.where: Terminal: agi projects list, then agi projects link <project>

labels.text: Operate on this repository instead of the current directory

S9.07.needs: a code repository folder on this computer
S9.07.note: A path flag, not a picker. The repository is checked to be a directory and no list or URL entry was found.
steps: In a terminal, type agi -C followed by the path of a code repository, then press Enter to start a session.
Ask the agent which folder it is working in, or check the session header.
Compare: the session works in the folder you typed. Only a folder path is accepted; no list or URL choice was found.

S9.10.needs: a task that asks for a tool approval
S9.10.note: Only tool-approval scopes were found. No scope choice for API keys or site automation was found.
steps: Start a task that asks to run a command, such as a shell command.
When the Tool Approval box appears, press the right arrow to move through Yes, No, Allow Session and Always allow.
Read the description under the selected button.
Compare: Yes runs it once, Allow Session lasts until the session ends, and Always allow saves a permanent rule.
S9.10.where: Tool Approval box, shown when the agent asks to run a tool

labels.text: Create a cron schedule that runs in AGI cloud.

S9.12.note: No once, daily, weekly or monthly choice was found; the user must write the cron expression.
steps: In a terminal, type agi schedules create --name test --schedule "0 9 * * *" --prompt "say hello" and press Enter.
Read the schedule summary the command prints.
Compare: the schedule runs on the cron cadence you typed. The only recurrence input is a 5-field cron expression.

S9.15.note: The table is shown, but no sortable column header was found.
steps: In the message box, type /models and press Enter.
Read the table of models and its column headers.
Compare: the table has headers. No sort control was found in the code, so check that sorting is missing.
S9.15.where: Type /models and press Enter in the message box

S9.17.needs: a signed-in AGI account with images in its Library
S9.17.note: Listing and downloading exist; a browsable gallery with a larger viewer was not found.
steps: In a terminal, type agi library --kind image and press Enter to list your images.
Type agi library download <id> to save one file, using an id from the list.
Compare: the list shows your images. No gallery or larger viewer was found; show prints text only.
S9.17.where: Terminal: agi library --kind image (lists your items)

S9.19.note: Steps are shown in order with state; no per-step duration was found in the code.
steps: Send a message that makes the agent run several tools, such as reading files.
Watch the tool rows appear in the chat in order.
Compare: each row shows a state glyph and turns to the check mark when done. Per-step time was not found; only the spinner shows elapsed time for the whole turn.
S9.19.where: Chat transcript while the agent runs tools

S9.23.needs: a first launch, or a machine where setup is not complete
S9.23.note: The wizard has no name step; sign-in is one of the auth choices. /setup exists in the non-TUI command path (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs).
steps: Run agi in an interactive terminal on a setup that has not been completed.
Read the Welcome banner, then Trust This Directory, then the auth list (Skip for now is the last choice).
Choose Select Model and then Select Reasoning Level, and press Enter at the end.
Compare: setup completes and a Setup completed marker is written. No name step was found.
S9.23.where: First launch: run agi in a terminal before setup is complete

S9.26.needs: a chat with at least one prompt sent
S9.26.note: The list shows prompts that made checkpoints; I did not confirm a time for each one in the code.
steps: Send at least one prompt, then type /rewind and press Enter.
Use the up and down arrows to choose a prompt, then press Enter.
Choose Restore code and conversation, Restore conversation or Restore code, then compare what came back.
S9.26.where: Type /rewind and press Enter in the message box (opens the Rewind box)

S9.27.note: /diff panel is a separate read-only view of changes beside the chat.
steps: In a repository with uncommitted changes, type /diff-review and press Enter.
Use the up and down arrows to move between files, and Page Up or Page Down to scroll the diff.
Press y, n or s for each file, then Enter to finish.
Compare: added and removed lines are marked in the Diff Review box before you decide.
S9.27.where: Type /diff-review and press Enter in the message box (in a repository with changes)

S9.29.needs: a signed-in AGI account (other accounts see an Unavailable line)
S9.29.note: Readable as text. Assistive-tech behaviour was not checked.
steps: In the message box, type /usage and press Enter.
Look under Account usage for the lines 5-hour window, Weekly and Monthly.
Compare: each line shows the percent used and when it resets. The output is text lines; no graphic bar was found.
S9.29.where: Type /usage in the message box, or run agi usage in a terminal

S9.30.note: Shown as text lines inside Account usage, not a separate card.
steps: In the message box, type /usage and press Enter.
Find the Purchased credits line under Account usage.
Find the Add credits line below it.
Compare: the balance and an add-credits link are shown together. If the server reports no credits, the line reads Credits: not reported by this server.
S9.30.where: Type /usage in the message box, or run agi usage in a terminal

S9.31.note: Scopes listed are allow, ask, deny, session and workspace. Expected says plain language; not confirmed.
steps: In the message box, type /permissions and press Enter.
Read the Permissions: header and the rules listed under it.
Type /permissions allow or /permissions ask to view one scope.
Compare: the rules are shown for allow, ask, deny and session. The output is a rule list; no plain-language summary was found.
S9.31.where: Type /permissions and press Enter in the message box

S9.32.note: Code says No skips the call and the agent continues, not that the run stops.
steps: Start a task that runs a shell command that is not already allowed.
Read the Tool Approval box to see the action it names.
Move with the left and right arrows to Yes or No, then press Enter.
Compare: Yes lets the run continue; No skips that call and the agent carries on, as its description says.
S9.32.where: Tool Approval box, shown when a task needs consent

S9.33.needs: a signed-in AGI account (connectors help: /connectors in chat shows policy text)
S9.33.note: Not a card in chat. The card's list is in the terminal command.
steps: In a terminal, type agi connectors and press Enter.
Read the line for each connector: connected since a date, or needs reconnecting with a link.
Type agi connectors disconnect <connector> to remove one (it asks first).
Compare: the state shown matches connected, needs reconnecting, or Available to connect. No separate expired label was found.
S9.33.where: Terminal: agi connectors (lists connectors and their state)

S9.35.note: A single spinner line, not a card. Steps done is not shown in code.
steps: Send a prompt that takes a while, such as one that runs several tools.
Watch the spinner line: it shows the verb, the elapsed seconds, and still working after about 10 seconds.
If an approval is needed, the line reads Waiting for your approval.
Compare: the line updates while the task runs. No count of steps done was found.
S9.35.where: Chat, the spinner line while a task runs

S9.38.note: Ctrl+P can be changed in keybindings. Typing / in an empty box also opens it. Lists commands; destinations were not confirmed.
steps: With the message box empty, press Ctrl+P.
The Commands box opens. Type part of a command name, such as model.
Use the arrows to pick, then press Enter.
Compare: the list narrows as you type, and Enter runs the highlighted command.
S9.38.where: Ctrl+P (default) with the message box empty
